gap: No result ChatGPT got states Consumer Reports' lab verdicts on the 120/240 V inverter generators it tested. The Honda EU7000iS 'handled surges very well' and was 'fairly quiet from a distance of 23 feet'. The Westinghouse iGen8200TFc 'could not handle surges well'. The Champion 201176 was 'fairly noisy from a distance of 23 feet; we recommend hearing protection'. CR found all three gave 'especially clean power'.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Consumer Reports inverter-generator category page (c200149). Fetched without a membership, it shows navigation only, with no per-model findings. I also checked the cited Lights On Labs page, which says 'We haven't tested these units ourselves' and uses only spec-sheet numbers, with the EU7000iS as its only 240 V model. homewelder.com says 'I have not run any of these generators myself', and rightgenerator.com says it uses 'provided specifications… rather than independent testing'. None of them shows a lab result for any split-phase inverter. CR's per-model pages are a separate click from the cited category page, so a reader of the cited result does not see them. That is why this scores 2 and not 3. None of ChatGPT's four cheaper cards (ecoGen10000, Champion 201417, WEN TF1050iX, WEN DF680iX) has a named measurement I could find.
decides: CR's lab backs the Honda EU7000iS as the premium split-phase pick: more than enough power, surges handled very well, clean power, fairly quiet at 23 ft. Among the cheaper split-phase inverters CR tested, the Westinghouse iGen8200TFc is quiet but 'could not handle surges well', which matters for well pumps and AC compressors. The Champion 201176 handles surges but CR rates it 'fairly noisy' at 23 ft. ChatGPT's value picks (ecoGen10000, 201417, TF1050iX, DF680iX) have no named lab or reviewer measurement I could find, so their THD and noise rest on maker claims alone. The page can say: if you need proven surge handling at 240 V, the only CR-verified choice is the Honda (or the louder Champion 201176).
